subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should cron jobs get their own `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` policy, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or keep the current per-job `toolsAllow` model with targeted delivery safeguards?
rationale: The choice defines a new scheduled-run tool-access boundary and public config contract, so automation should not choose defaults or precedence across existing policy layers.

options.title: Add cron-scoped policy
options.body: Introduce a first-class cron tool-policy layer with explicit precedence against global, agent, sandbox, subagent, and per-job `toolsAllow` policy.

options.title: Inherit subagent policy
options.body: Reuse `tools.subagents.tools` for cron runs to reduce config surface, accepting that subagents and scheduled jobs become coupled policy domains.

options.title: Keep per-job only
options.body: Do not add a global cron policy; rely on per-job `toolsAllow`, docs, and delivery safeguards for scheduled-run tool restriction.

recommendation.title: Add cron-scoped policy
recommendation.body: Introduce a first-class cron tool-policy layer with explicit precedence against global, agent, sandbox, subagent, and per-job `toolsAllow` policy.
